name: Whistled language interpretation (Silbo Gomero)
open_problem: Whistled registers like Silbo Gomero compress a full spoken language into a tiny set of pitch/continuity contrasts (only ~2-4 whistled vowels and 4-10 consonants), and decoding them back into speech is done entirely by trained human ears in real time; there is no robust tool to transcribe or translate whistled speech, and the practice survives in only a handful of communities worldwide.
verbatim_quote: Silbo replaces each vowel or consonant with a whistling sound.

name: Sign language transcription and glossing (no standard notation)
open_problem: Signed languages have no commonly accepted written or transcription system, so linguists hand-gloss video utterance-by-utterance using ad hoc systems (Stokoe, HamNoSys, glosses); annotation is slow, inconsistent across labs, and there is no widely usable automatic notation/transcription pipeline for the spatial-simultaneous structure of signs.
verbatim_quote: There is no commonly accepted transcription system for describing the form of signs.

name: Prosody and intonation labeling (ToBI)
open_problem: Labeling the intonation/prosody of speech with the standard ToBI system is extraordinarily slow expert manual work (roughly 100-200x real time per minute of audio) and even trained labelers achieve only moderate inter-transcriber agreement, leaving most speech corpora unannotated for prosody.
verbatim_quote: A ToBI prosodic labeling of speech typically takes even experienced labelers from 100 to 200 times real time.

name: Tone-language transcription in phonetic fieldwork
open_problem: Documenting the tone systems of under-described African and Asian languages relies on manually marking pitch height and contour (e.g. numeric 1-5 notation) by ear; transcribers need months of specialised training, the work is slow and costly, and it is racing against the rapid disappearance of endangered tone languages.
verbatim_quote: Current phonetic fieldwork relies on manual effort, resulting in substantial time and financial costs, especially challenging for endangered languages that are rapidly disappearing with limited funding.

name: Dialectology fieldwork and linguistic-atlas compilation
open_problem: Traditional dialect mapping still depends on painstaking in-person fieldwork (questionnaires, hand phonetic transcription, isogloss drawing) targeting specific NORM speakers; compiling a linguistic atlas is slow, expensive and labour-intensive, so most regions and dialect continua remain only partially surveyed.
verbatim_quote: The preparation and compilation of linguistic atlases is a difficult, costly, voluminous, and time-consuming job.

name: Cuneiform tablet reading backlog (Assyriology)
open_problem: Of the hundreds of thousands of excavated cuneiform tablets, the large majority have never been read or published because transliteration requires years of training and only a few hundred qualified experts exist worldwide; the script has no word spacing and signs are polyvalent, making automated reading still nascent and unreliable.
verbatim_quote: An estimated half a million tablets are held in museums across the world, but comparatively few of these are published.

name: Historical linguistic reconstruction via the comparative method
open_problem: Reconstructing proto-languages is done by hand: linguists identify cognate sets, line up sound correspondences, and propose proto-forms following phonetic rules; this is slow expert judgement work with little tooling, and it breaks down beyond ~8,000-10,000 years as cognates become unrecognisable.
verbatim_quote: Reconstruction becomes unreliable beyond roughly 8,000 to 10,000 years, as sound changes accumulate to the point where cognates are no longer recognizable.

name: Snakebite responsible-species identification
open_problem: Choosing the right antivenom depends on knowing which snake bit the patient, but the snake is rarely seen, victim descriptions are misleading, and frontline rural hospital staff are usually not trained to identify the biting species even when it is brought in dead - so antivenom choice is often guesswork in exactly the low-resource settings where snakebite kills most.
verbatim_quote: In many cases of envenoming following snake bite, the snake responsible for the accident remains unidentified; this frequently results in difficulty deciding which antivenom to administer to the systemically-envenomed victim, especially when only monospecific antivenoms are available.

name: Chronic wound assessment (visual and manual measurement)
open_problem: Tracking whether a chronic wound is healing relies on a clinician's naked-eye judgement of size and tissue type plus manual ruler measurement; this is highly subjective, varies with the clinician's experience, and manual area estimates can deviate enormously (up to 40-75%) from true wound size, with poor inter-rater reliability.
verbatim_quote: Wound assessment and measurement depend on visual examination, which can be highly subjective and dependent on the clinician's experience.

name: Ethnobotanical / traditional herbal medicine knowledge documentation
open_problem: Vast bodies of traditional herbal-remedy knowledge held by healers are undocumented and passed only by word of mouth; with the spread of modern medicine this knowledge is being eroded and lost generation by generation, and capturing it depends on slow manual ethnobotanical surveys.
verbatim_quote: Most cultures possess a huge store of undocumented traditional knowledge of applying herbal remedies in the treatment of diseases.

name: Ethnoveterinary medicine documentation and dosing
open_problem: Smallholder farmers across Africa and Asia treat livestock with plant-based home remedies where vets are unavailable, but the practice suffers from poor knowledge of application rates/dosage, inadequate diagnosis, and almost no documentation or standardisation - an indigenous knowledge system with essentially no decision-support tooling.
verbatim_quote: Some farmers have failed to use ethnoveterinary medicine due to poor knowledge of application rates (dosage), inadequate diagnosis, lack of documentation and side effects of the concoctions.

name: Prosthetic socket fitting (craft skill)
open_problem: Getting a comfortable prosthetic socket fit is a hand craft: the prosthetist casts the residual limb, manually 'rectifies' the positive mould, and iterates check sockets by feel; the result is time-consuming, expensive and heavily dependent on the individual prosthetist's skill, with little objective guidance on where to add or relieve pressure.
verbatim_quote: The process is time-consuming expensive and heavily dependent on the individual skills of the prosthetist.

name: Observational gait analysis in clinic
open_problem: Most clinical gait assessment is done by a therapist watching the patient walk and visually estimating joint angles and step parameters with no instrumentation; reliability is poor, results depend on the evaluator's expertise, and inter-rater agreement is low - yet instrumented labs are rarely available, so the subjective method dominates practice.
verbatim_quote: Reliability of observational analysis is poor, and therapists should be encouraged to use objective measures to give a more representative account of the gait pattern.

name: Partograph-based labour monitoring in low-resource midwifery
open_problem: In low-resource maternity settings the partograph (manual plotting of cervical dilatation and fetal/maternal signs against alert/action lines) is the main tool to catch obstructed or abnormal labour, but correct use is labour-intensive, completion rates are low, and there are too few skilled attendants - so warning signs are missed where maternal/newborn mortality is highest.
verbatim_quote: The correct and effective use of the partograph is labour intensive even with the requisite skills, making it unfriendly to use in situations where the delivery rates are high with few skilled attendants.
